items.t: Spy targeting Nvidia CEO was alleged China intelligence service recruit: Report
sum: The Chinese businesswoman, with whom Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang had alleged ties, was recruited as a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, The New York Times reported, citing a memo circulated among policymakers in the Trump administration.

On Friday, three House Republican committee chairs have asked Nvidia CEO to address, behind closed doors, the reported links with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of providing information to Beijing, Axios reported.

A top executive at a Singapore-based data centre firm named Megaspeed faced intense scrutiny over potential involvement in diverting advanced Nvidia AI chips towards China, as outlined in a report by The New York Times. US authorities reportedly determined that she operated as a Chinese intelligence asset, transmitting information back to Beijing.

According to the report, surveillance of the executive, identified as Chinese national Alice Huang or Huang Le, revealed that she maintained a close association with Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.

US President Donald Trump had expressed uncertainty over his confidence in Jensen Huang as an adviser on US technology policy amid the alleged links with the Chinese businesswoman, as per the Washington Post.
Speaking to reporters at his annual Halloween party at Mar-a-Lago in Florida, Trump said he wanted to continue backing Huang but would wait for further information before concluding.

"I would like to say yes. I mean, unless we find out something to the contrary," Trump said when asked whether he still had confidence in Huang as an adviser. "I've always found Jensen Huang to be very aboveboard. But you know, you're dealing in a very complex issue," he added.

Australia Recruit Mike Hussey As Consultant For Ashes And 2027 World Cup
sum: Mike Hussey was Friday appointed a consultant coach to the Australian team for next year's blockbuster Ashes series against England and the 2027 World Cup.
The former Australian batsmen revealed in August that England's new red-ball coach, Stephen Fleming, had informally approached him to be their Test batting mentor.

But the 51-year-old knocked back the audacious offer and has instead committed himself to helping his home nation arrest a batting crisis highlighted by their recent 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa.

Hussey, known as "Mr Cricket" for his technical expertise, will also provide coaching assistance during this month's home T20 series against England and the subsequent four-Test series against New Zealand.
He will additionally work with Australia during the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where cricket is on the agenda, and the T20 World Cup in 2028.
"I am extremely excited about being a part of the team in a more formal and meaningful role in the coming years," said Hussey, who played more than 300 matches for Australia across all formats.
"This team has achieved so much in recent times, to which I hope I can add value to the coaching and playing groups ahead of what will be an exciting and challenging period."

Uber’s profit forecast disappoints as driver shortages, Middle East conflict hurt
sum: Uber UBER-N forecast adjusted profit below Wall Street expectations on Wednesday, as driver shortages, higher fuel costs and the Middle East conflict weighed on ride-hailing growth in markets ranging from India and Brazil to Canada.

The company is responding by spending more to recruit and retain drivers, a cost that will be watched closely because it comes as the company also funds a major push into autonomous vehicles and a string of acquisitions.
Shares of the ride-hailing company were down nearly 2 per cent in premarket trading.
Uber forecast fourth-quarter adjusted profit of 95 US cents to 99 US cents per share, below estimates of US$1.06 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG.
The company said the Middle East conflict was a 75 basis-point drag on Mobility bookings growth and that it assumes a 100 basis-point hit in the fourth quarter.
“Elevated fuel prices and tighter driver availability weighed on supply growth in several international markets,” said CEO Dara Khosrowshahi in prepared remarks.
“We also saw an impact in Canada from tighter immigration flows, and the market is currently meaningfully undersupplied.”

TCS Shares Rise 4% As Q2 Profit Beats Estimates, AI Revenue Crosses $3.1 Bn
sum: Annualised revenue from AI services crosses USD 3.1 billion, taking the business beyond 10 per cent of its overall revenue run rate

Shares of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) rose more than 2 per cent in early trade on Friday, as investors focused on stronger-than-expected September-quarter profit and growing artificial intelligence (AI) revenue, setting aside near-term concerns over the US suspension of the company from its employment-based green card programme.

The stock opened 0.48 per cent higher at Rs 2,086 apiece on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) before climbing 2.12 per cent to Rs 2,120.10. The positive reaction followed TCS reporting a 4 per cent sequential increase in net profit to Rs 13,884 crore for the second quarter, ahead of analyst estimates tracked by Bloomberg.

Revenue rose 1.3 per cent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 73,188 crore, broadly in line with expectations. Earnings before interest and tax increased 1.4 per cent to Rs 17,553 crore, while the operating margin edged up to 24 per cent from 23.95 per cent in the June quarter.

Investor attention also centred on TCS’ expanding AI business and a series of strategic partnerships announced during the quarter. The company said annualised revenue from AI services had crossed USD 3.1 billion, taking the business beyond 10 per cent of its overall revenue run rate.

Among its key announcements was a five-year strategic partnership with Porsche AG, under which TCS will acquire the entire stake in MHP, the German automaker’s management and IT consulting subsidiary. TCS also agreed to take over Best Buy’s Global Capability Centre in India and convert it into a dedicated AI Capability Centre focused on developing advanced AI-powered solutions.

TCS Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director K Krithivasan described the Porsche and Best Buy agreements as a new category of transformation partnerships, aimed at building platforms that can deliver AI-driven value at scale.

Drinkwitz shares positive update in heart transplant search for Mizzou freshman OL
sum: COLUMBIA, Mo. (KCTV) - Missouri head football coach Eli Drinkwitz shared a positive update early Thursday morning regarding the search for a heart transplant for Tigers freshman offensive lineman Johnnie ‘DJ’ Jones.
“Last night, DJ received his heart transplant, and his surgery went well,” Drinkwitz shared in a post on X. “He is now recovering.”
Drinkwitz continued: “We are incredibly grateful for the medical team who cared for DJ and for the donor and donor family whose extraordinary gift made this possible.”
Jones, an 18-year-old from Bradenton, Florida, had been hospitalized at the Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida, Drinkwitz revealed earlier in the week.

Mizzou’s training staff initially detected an issue with Jones’ heart over the summer during freshman intake testing. A second opinion was sought at the Mayo Clinic after Drinkwitz said two weeks of observation didn’t result in a resolution.
On Tuesday, asked Mizzou fans to join in that prayer, saying the 18-year-old “needs help in a hurry.” Now, Jones got that help, and is recovering from surgery.
Jones graduated from Venice High School on Florida’s Gulf Coast and signed with Missouri as a four-star recruit.

Japan’s Nikkei Rises as AI Catch-Up Rally Offsets Yield Worries
sum: The Nikkei stock benchmark gained after a three-day holiday as Tokyo’s market caught up with a global AI-led rally. Climbing bond yields and a rise in oil prices weighed on broader risk appetite, however.

The Nikkei 225 rose 1.8% to 66,167.25 as of 10:09 a.m. in Tokyo, while the broader Topix rose 0.2% to 4,097.42. Chip-related firms like Ibiden Co. and Socionext Inc. were among the Nikkei’s best performers, while software names like Baycurrent Inc. and Recruit Holdings Co. weighed. The Topix was led by electronics and machinery makers, with banks and services weak.

While Japan was closed for its Silver Week holiday, the global AI trade gathered steam thanks to early signs of success for Meta Platforms Inc.’s new AI agent and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s unveiling of what it calls China’s most powerful AI chip. The Nasdaq 100 hit a fresh record high on Tuesday, although US equities pared gains on Wednesday amid inflation concerns.
“We expect the semiconductor-heavy Nikkei 225 to take cues from the strength in global technology stocks,” said Hu You, a senior research analyst at iFast Financial in Singapore.

Japan’s broad range of chip material makers makes it well positioned to benefit from renewed bullishness around AI, said You. Ibiden is a particular winner as the chip package substrate maker is set to gain from the increasing complexity of AI semiconductors and demand for advanced packaging, she added.
But volatility in the yen, which is trading around 158 to the dollar, is likely to keep investors cautious, You said.
Climbing global bond yields are another concern. Japan’s benchmark 10-year government bond yield rose eight basis points to 3.055% on Thursday morning, tracking moves in the Treasury market.

Nikkei extends gains, briefly tops 65,800 as U.S. semiconductor rally over holiday weekend provides tailwind
sum: The Nikkei Stock Average opened higher on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on September 24, extending its winning streak. The opening level was 65,476.44, up 457.49 points from the September 18 close before the Silver Week holiday. After the open, gains widened to more than 600 points, and the index briefly surged over 800 points to the 65,800 level in early trading. The buying momentum that swept through AI and semiconductor stocks in U.S. markets during the holiday carried over into related names on the Tokyo exchange.

Among semiconductor-related stocks, Advantest, Tokyo Electron, and Ibiden opened sharply higher. SoftBank Group, whose U.K.-based chip design subsidiary Arm Holdings posted significant gains during the holiday, briefly surged more than 7%. Fast Retailing, a heavyweight contributor to the index, also traded firmly. On the downside, Toyota Motor and Sony Group edged lower, while Recruit Holdings, Mitsubishi Corp., and banking stocks including Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group declined. The Tokyo Stock Price Index (TOPIX) rebounded.

During the holiday period, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite hit a three-and-a-half-month high on September 21 in U.S. markets. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX), which tracks major semiconductor-related names, climbed roughly 8% from September 18 through September 23. In Japan, buying was concentrated in high-priced semiconductor stocks that carry significant weight in the Nikkei average.

The decline in crude oil prices also supported investor sentiment. NYMEX crude oil futures settled in the $92-per-barrel range on September 23. Prices had hovered around $100 before Japan's holiday, but excessive concerns over Middle East supply disruptions eased, bringing prices lower. The fading risk of corporate earnings deterioration and inflation concerns stemming from high oil prices has reinforced the bullish stance.

Developments surrounding U.S.-China trade negotiations also provided a tailwind for the market. Ahead of the U.S.-China summit on September 24, U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent reportedly said on September 23 that the two sides had agreed to extend the trade war ceasefire—set to expire on November 10—by two months.

sum: Recruit Holdings (JP3970300004) reported 2,702,500 share repurchases for September on October 1, 2026, while Recruit stock was trading at EUR 100.05 at Lang & Schwarz on October 9, 2026, up 3.60 percent versus the prior close of EUR 96.57. According to Recruit Holdings, the company spent JPY 43.2 billion on the September purchases.

The September purchases lifted cumulative repurchases since April 1, 2026 to 16,356,000 shares, or 25.56 percent of the authorized maximum. The total purchase amount reached JPY 177.7 billion, equal to 50.76 percent of the program's JPY 350.0 billion ceiling, according to Recruit Holdings.

On March 31, 2026, the board authorized purchases of up to 64,000,000 shares. On August 7, 2026, Recruit reported first-quarter revenue of JPY 1.045 trillion, up 18.90 percent year over year, while operating income rose 66.10 percent to JPY 255.4 billion, according to the Recruit Holdings earnings release.

The same report showed profit attributable to owners of the parent rising 67.50 percent to JPY 202.6 billion in the first quarter. Recruit also raised fiscal-year 2026 guidance to JPY 4.230 trillion of revenue and JPY 945.0 billion of operating income, compared with prior guidance of JPY 4.030 trillion and JPY 787.0 billion.

Recruit's investor-relations calendar lists November 11, 2026 for second-quarter fiscal-year 2026 results. The buyback authorization runs until November 30, 2026, or until its share or spending limit is reached, according to Recruit Holdings investor relations.

At Lang & Schwarz, Recruit stock was trading at EUR 100.05 on October 9, 2026 at 12:40 p.m. CEST, up 3.60 percent versus the prior close of EUR 96.57. Michigan NFL Draft Stock Watch: Bryce Underwood Tumbles Down Boards
sum: Bryce Underwood came to Ann Arbor for $15 million. And from the jump, nothing less than an eventual bona fide superstar under center has been expected by Michigan faithful and analysts alike. It was simply impossible to project Underwood through collegiate coaching with the frame, speed, arm strength, and work ethic he possesses without arriving at a glowing prognosis for how his career will develop.
Entering college as the number one overall recruit and with everything seemingly working in his favor, Underwood had been a long presumed early selection of the 2028 NFL Draft. Why wouldn’t he be?
Well, his performance against Western Michigan provides a couple clues.

It’s important to preface this section with the note that single collegiate performances rarely overhaul a given prospect’s professional outlook, especially for athletes still years removed from entering the draft. Yes, NFL franchises evaluate talents based on in-game performances, but they also place as much, if not more, emphasis on measurables and future potential when examining a player. Normally, 48 minute snippets of a player’s resume won’t completely change the calculus.

Yet that’s exactly what Bryce Underwood’s season opening performance has done. His dud against Western Michigan did not change how tall he is, how agile he is, or how hard he throws a football. What it did do is raise the question of whether he can improve.

That’s the real issue with the Western Michigan game. Underwood had had an offseason of presumably the first fully competent coaching he’s received in college to make necessary strides from an up and down freshman campaign. Yet such strides were not taken. Rather, Underwood looked skittish in the pocket, stared down receivers, and time after time made the incorrect throw against basic coverages. Regression, not improvement, was the story of the day.

In June, reputable mock drafts of the 2028 draft featured Underwood as the first selection off the board. Following the season opener, Underwood slipped all the way to a projected 47th by some prognosticators' estimations.

Xingyu Automotive Lighting's H1 net profit falls 5% but still pays 56.64 million yuan dividend; fallout from graduate-recruit layoff controversy lingers
sum: On the evening of August 26, Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems (601799.SS) disclosed its 2026 interim report. During the reporting period, the company achieved revenue of 6.884 billion yuan (approximately $1.0 billion), up 1.87% year-on-year; net profit attributable to shareholders of the listed company was 669 million yuan (approximately $99.7 million), down 5.26% year-on-year. Despite earnings pressure, the company still plans to distribute a cash dividend of 2.00 yuan per 10 shares to all shareholders, totaling approximately 56.64 million yuan (approximately $8.4 million). The proposal was approved unanimously by the board with 7 votes.

Less than a month before this earnings release, this leading Chinese automotive lighting company had just weathered a public relations storm that swept across the internet. In early August, Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems, citing "business difficulties" and "poor market conditions," summoned 2026 fresh graduates who had been on the job for only one month for group interviews, offering them two options: "voluntary resignation" or "reassignment to frontline operator positions." Ultimately, 107 people had their labor contracts terminated. After an investigation, the Changzhou Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau reported that the company's negotiation process was "crude and rigid, lacking sufficient and effective communication," and suspended the HR director from duty.

Judging from the interim report data, Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems faced a classic "revenue growth without profit growth" dilemma in the first half. On the revenue side, the company undertook R&D projects for 59 vehicle models' lighting systems and achieved mass production for 46 models during the period, both increases from the same period last year, driving modest revenue growth. On the profit side, however, the company was squeezed by weak domestic passenger vehicle sales, underperforming volumes for certain supported models, and rising raw material prices, resulting in a 5.26% year-on-year decline in net profit attributable to shareholders.
Changes in the expense structure further confirm the source of operating pressure.

USC Running Back Waymond Jordan Shares Candid Insights Into Injury Recovery
sum: Senior running back Waymond Jordan sat down with Trojans Live ahead of USC's season opener on Aug. 29. During the interview, Jordan opened up about fall camp, his health and how he spent his time recovering and the leadership of Jayden Maiava.
“I feel amazing. Real confident about the year and just ready to get going,” Jordan said about his final year at Southern Cal.

Jordan had spent the majority of spring ball on the sideline due to a cleanup procedure on his injured ankle. By the time the Trojans’ summer sessions were beginning, he was cleared to be a full-go participant. For fall camp, the senior back has carried zero restrictions.
A huge factor in Jordan’s healthy fall camp has been the Bloom Football Performance Center.

“I think the resources are infinite. The recovery room, the training room, just everything. It's nothing that we don't have there so just having all those resources basically at our hand, at will, is amazing,” Jordan said about the Bloom. “I mean I came from junior college, so [the John McKay Center] was a lot for me. I'm still thankful for the upgrade.”

The new red light therapy beds have been Jordan’s go-to equipment since the facility opened up to the team. The beds use low-level wavelengths of red light to promote cell repair and regeneration, ease minor muscle soreness and joint stiffness, reduce inflammation and boost skin health.
“I know it helps the joints and muscles recover a lot…It keeps me fresh. I also invested in red light for at home.”

Recruit Holdings Hits Limit Up as Strong Earnings and Target Price Hike to ¥17,100 Fuel Bullish Sentiment
sum: Shares of Recruit Holdings (6098.T), a major Japanese staffing and human resources services company, hit their daily limit up on August 10. The surge came after the company's first-quarter (April-June) results for the fiscal year ending March 2026, released the previous weekend, significantly beat market expectations, and a major European brokerage raised its target price by 33.6% to ¥17,100, triggering concentrated buying from investors.

The company's first-quarter operating profit expanded sharply, rising 66.1% year-on-year to ¥255.4 billion (approximately $1.6 billion). Market expectations had been for just under ¥200 billion (approximately $1.3 billion), making the magnitude of the upside surprise particularly impactful for investors. The full-year operating profit forecast was also revised upward, from the previous ¥787 billion (approximately $5.0 billion) to ¥945 billion (approximately $6.0 billion), representing a 49.9% increase from the prior fiscal year. This new guidance far exceeds the market consensus, which was seen at just over ¥800 billion (approximately $5.1 billion).

The HR Technology segment was the primary driver of the strong results. While the total number of job listings on the job search engine Indeed remained sluggish, the paid job advertising service "Premium Sponsored Jobs" gained strong momentum, particularly in the U.S. market, contributing significantly to revenue growth.

In response to the robust earnings, a major European brokerage reaffirmed its "Buy" rating on Recruit Holdings on August 7, while raising its target price from ¥12,800 to ¥17,100. Based on the consensus rating of 4.93 from 14 analysts as of August 6, which already reflected a bullish stance, and a consensus target price of ¥13,286, the new target represents a bullish assessment that exceeds the market average by more than 28%.

The stock reacted to this double dose of positive news, with buying pushing the price up to the daily limit. The market has once again recognized the earnings power of the HR Technology segment, and expectations for further full-year earnings upside are also rising.

Mekhi Robertson commits to Merrimack, becoming the first nationally-ranked recruit in program history
sum: Mekhi Robertson will become the latest in a long line of talented guards to play for Joe Gallo at Merrimack after announcing his commitment to the Warriors on Wednesday.
Robertson is the first four-star prospect and the first nationally ranked recruit in Merrimack history. The South Pemberton, N.J., native is ranked No. 137 overall in the Class of 2027.

Robertson will play this season at The Master’s Academy International in Stow. West Virginia, N.C. State, Oklahoma State and Mississippi State were among the programs pursuing him, but Gallo and his staff ultimately landed the highly touted prospect.

The significance of this commitment shouldn’t be overlooked. Ranked directly ahead of Robertson at No. 136 is Saint Louis commit Jimmy McKinney. Colorado State commit Luke Howery is ranked No. 138, while Kansas State commit Kameron Cooper is just behind him.
He shared his thoughts on his selection with the folks over at 247 sports.

“I have a lot of trust in Coach Gallo and the entire coaching staff,” Robertson said. “Their resume speaks for itself, and the success of the previous guards who’ve come through Merrimack and gone on to do great things says a lot about how they operate and how they develop their guards.
“I know this is the right place for me to continue growing both on and off the court.”

Recruit Holdings (TSE:6098) Stock Could Be A Bargain Below Fair Value
sum: Make better investment decisions with Simply Wall St's easy, visual tools that give you a competitive edge.

Recruit Holdings stock has returned 151.0% over the last three years, and the current valuation setup now shows a different kind of tension: the intrinsic value estimate from a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) points to meaningful upside compared with the share price, while the broader valuation checks are more mixed.

- A 151.0% return over three years puts Recruit Holdings among the stronger performers. This naturally raises the question of how much upside may reasonably remain for new money going in at today's price.

- For long term valuation, Recruit Holdings can benefit if it continues to convert revenue into reliable cash flows. However, sentiment could weaken if investors start to question the durability of its growth or its ability to reinvest efficiently.

- The company screens as undervalued on both a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view and market multiples. Yet the broader checks are only mixed, with Recruit Holdings passing 3 of 6 valuation tests on Simply Wall St's scorecard at 3/6, which points to some areas that do not look outright cheap.
The issue now is whether the current price already captures most of the good news, or if Recruit Holdings still offers an attractive margin of safety against its intrinsic value estimate.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) approach values Recruit Holdings by projecting its future cash generation and discounting it back to today. On this model, the latest twelve month free cash flow sits at about ¥601.0b, and the projections assume growing cash flows rather than a shrinking business, which supports the use of a 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity framework.
